column2: The small and large intestines together measure roughly 750 centimetres in an adult.
Adult men typically have 5–6 litres of blood and adult women 4–5 litres.
A commonly used estimate is 550 litres of oxygen consumed per adult per day; inhaled volume is greater.
The salivary glands produce about 0.5–1.5 litres of saliva per day.
A widely quoted estimate is 60,000 miles of blood vessels, approximately 96,600 kilometres.
The Chronicles of Narnia comprises seven books, published from 1950 to 1956.
The main Harry Potter series comprises seven books, published from 1997 to 2007.
Don Quixote appeared in two parts, in 1605 and 1615.
The Lord of the Rings originally appeared in three volumes in 1954–1955.
The usual count is 39 Shakespeare plays, depending on which collaborations are included.
Johann Carolus's Relation, published in Strasbourg in 1605, is generally considered the first printed newspaper.
The Bactrian camel has two humps; the dromedary has one.
Adult king penguins weigh about 9–18 kilograms.
Crabs have ten legs, including the front pair bearing claws.
Male Asian elephants average approximately 4,000 kilograms; females about 2,700.
Wombats usually weigh 20–35 kilograms.
Sperm whales can dive deeper than 2,000 metres while hunting squid.
The garden snail can reach about 1.3 centimetres per second, nearly 50 metres per hour.
Dogs have 78 chromosomes, arranged in 39 pairs.
Woodlice and other isopods have seven pairs of walking legs: fourteen in total.
Madagascar has over a hundred lemur species, found nowhere else in the wild.
Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026, bringing the total to 21 EU member states.
Euro notes and coins entered circulation in twelve countries on 1 January 2002.
The G20 includes nineteen countries, the European Union and, since 2023, the African Union.
Eight West African and six Central African countries use a CFA franc: fourteen in total.
Belgium's standard VAT rate is 21 percent.
Germany's standard VAT rate is 19 percent.
On 12 January 2009, Satoshi Nakamoto sent ten bitcoins to Hal Finney in the first bitcoin transaction.
Brazil comprises 26 states and one federal district.
McDonald's reported 41,822 restaurants worldwide at the end of 2023.
A US McDonald's cheeseburger contains about 31 grams of carbohydrate.
A US 355 ml can of Coca-Cola contains 39 grams of sugar.
Argentina is among the largest beef consumers, at around fifty kilograms per person per year, although consumption is falling.
A standard Dutch jenever glass holds 35 millilitres.
Brazil is the largest coffee producer and supplies approximately 35 percent of world coffee.
A 330 ml can of Coca-Cola contains 35 grams of sugar, equivalent to nearly nine 4-gram cubes.
Titanic (1997) won eleven Oscars, matching Ben-Hur and The Return of the King.
The 2019 HBO miniseries Chernobyl has five episodes.
Game of Thrones has 73 episodes across eight seasons.
The British version of The Office has twelve regular episodes and two Christmas specials: fourteen in total.
Back to the Future comprises three films, released in 1985, 1989 and 1990.
Before Resurrections, there were The Matrix (1999), Reloaded and Revolutions (both 2003).
Before Jurassic World, there were Jurassic Park (1993), The Lost World (1997) and Jurassic Park III (2001).
Avatar: The Way of Water runs for 192 minutes.
The Sopranos ran for six seasons from 1999 to 2007.
The US version of The Office ran for nine seasons from 2005 to 2013.
By summer 2026, 37 seasons had aired; season 38 began in autumn 2026.
Sean Connery played James Bond in six official films, from Dr. No to Diamonds Are Forever.
Greek mythology has nine Muses, daughters of Zeus and Mnemosyne.
According to the Gospels, Jesus chose twelve apostles.
Jewish tradition counts 613 mitzvot in the Torah: 248 commandments and 365 prohibitions.
The Twelve Olympians were the principal gods associated with Mount Olympus.
Cerberus is usually depicted as a three-headed dog.
Yggdrasil connects nine worlds in Norse mythology.
The Pont du Gard's lowest tier has six arches.
The bridge's arch consists of two parallel steel arch ribs, each with 28 panels.
The Eiffel Tower can expand by up to approximately 15 centimetres in hot weather.
The Colosseum had 80 entrances, including 76 numbered public entrances.
Construction of the Taj Mahal complex lasted approximately 21 years, from 1632 to around 1653.
An average stone block in the Great Pyramid weighs approximately 2.5 tonnes.
The Golden Gate Bridge's main span is 4,200 feet, or 1,280 metres.
Mexico City's metro totals 226.5 kilometres, including 200.9 kilometres of passenger routes.
The two main cables contain about 80,000 miles of wire, approximately 128,000 kilometres.
Four bronze lions lie at the foot of Nelson's Column.
Tokyo Tower is 333 metres tall.
The Brooklyn Bridge's towers are 84 metres tall.
The Van Brienenoord Bridge's arch spans 287 metres, rounding to 300 metres.
Istanbul's Blue Mosque has six minarets.
El Castillo has four stairways with 91 steps each.
The roof has 1,056,006 tiles, approximately one million.
The Eiffel Tower contains 7,300 tonnes of puddled iron.
The Eiffel Tower's total weight is approximately 10,100 tonnes.
Gran Torre Santiago has 62 above-ground floors and is 300 metres tall.
The UNESCO listing for Le Corbusier's work comprises seventeen buildings in seven countries.
Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt border the Mediterranean Sea.
There are approximately 1,350 potentially active volcanoes worldwide.
Amsterdam had 934,526 inhabitants on 1 January 2025 and just over 930,000 a year earlier.
Luxembourg had 660,809 inhabitants on 1 January 2023.
Geoscience Australia gives mainland Australia's coastline as approximately 35,900 kilometres.
Indonesia comprises over 17,000 islands.
Belgium has three regions: Flanders, Wallonia and Brussels-Capital.
Belgium's flag has three vertical bands: black, yellow and red.
The Sahara is roughly 1,300–1,900 kilometres wide north to south and 4,800 kilometres east to west.
The Niger is approximately 4,200 kilometres long.
The Rhine is approximately 1,230 kilometres long.
The Zambezi is 2,574 kilometres long.
The CIA World Factbook gives Norway's coastline, including fjords and islands, as 25,148 kilometres.
Brazil borders ten countries, including France through French Guiana.
Jordan and Israel border the Dead Sea, as does the West Bank.
Italy, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Albania border the Adriatic Sea.
Average flow over Niagara Falls is approximately 2,400 cubic metres per second, or 2.4 million litres.
Uluru rises 348 metres above its surroundings and 863 metres above sea level.
Kilimanjaro's highest summit is 5,895 metres above sea level.
Argentina's 2022 census counted just over 46 million inhabitants.
Chile has approximately twenty million inhabitants.
Peru has approximately 34 million inhabitants.
The People's Republic of China officially counts 23 provinces, including its claim to Taiwan.
All of India uses Indian Standard Time, UTC+5:30.
There are five Great Lakes: Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario.
The road distance from Amsterdam to Rome is approximately 1,650 kilometres.
D-Day was 6 June 1944; Paris was liberated on 25 August, eighty days later.
The Battle of Verdun lasted from 21 February to 18 December 1916, approximately 300 days.
Apartheid was introduced in 1948 and ended with the first free elections in 1994.
Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison, from 1962 to 1990.
A commonly quoted estimate is that approximately 2,000 people died in Pompeii in the AD 79 eruption.
Four US presidents were assassinated: Lincoln, Garfield, McKinley and Kennedy.
Columbus departed in 1492 with three ships: Santa María, Pinta and Niña.
Over 850 ships and boats took part in the Dunkirk evacuation.
The Greek fleet had approximately 370 triremes, less than half the Persian fleet.
India became independent of Britain on 15 August 1947.
China had sixty World Heritage Sites after the July 2025 inscriptions.
Rembrandt made approximately three hundred etchings.
Amsterdam has approximately eighty museums.
Van Gogh painted seven Arles versions: four in August 1888 and three repetitions in January 1889.
Rembrandt painted approximately forty self-portraits.
Sheep gestation averages 147 days, usually ranging from 142 to 152 days.
An average new European car contained approximately 200 kilograms of aluminium in 2022.
Over half of all steel is used in buildings and infrastructure.
China produced 1,019 million of the world's 1,888 million tonnes of crude steel in 2023, about 54 percent.
Lidl opened its 13,000th store in September 2026.
UNEP estimates that 19–23 million tonnes of plastic waste enter rivers, lakes and seas annually.
Approximately half of Earth's plant and animal species live in tropical rainforests.
Forests cover approximately 31 percent of the world's land area.
The OECD estimates that 22 percent of plastic waste was mismanaged in 2019.
A round brilliant has 57 facets, or 58 including a culet.
Eleven nominations for 2025 brought Beyoncé's career total to 99 Grammy nominations.
The Dom Tower's carillon has fifty bells.
The classic Beatles lineup had four members: Lennon, McCartney, Harrison and Starr.
Un Verano Sin Ti (2022) has 23 tracks.
A concert pedal harp has 47 strings.
A standard guitar has six strings.
Beethoven composed sixteen string quartets.
Michael Jackson released ten solo studio albums during his lifetime, from Got to Be There to Invincible.
The Life of a Showgirl (October 2025) is Taylor Swift's twelfth studio album, excluding Taylor's Version rerecordings.
Beaufort force 8 covers 62–74 kilometres per hour.
The Dutch Constitution has 142 articles.
The 1789 Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen has seventeen articles.
Peru has 25 regions, alongside the province of Lima.
Full accession by Bulgaria and Romania on 1 January 2025 brought Schengen membership to 29 countries.
Australia's House had 151 seats after the 2022 election and 150 after the 2025 election.
New Zealand's parliament normally has 120 seats; the 2023 election produced 123 because of additional seats.
Pizza Hut and Airrack made a 1,296.72-square-metre pizza in Los Angeles in 2023.
Guinness lists Thumbelina as the smallest horse ever, at 44.5 centimetres.
Bluey lived for 29 years and five months; Guinness withdrew Bobi's later record in 2024.
At the end of 2025, Ian and Stuart Paton held the record at 1,278.8 kilograms; it was broken in October 2026.
Horst Preisler completed 1,305 marathons or longer races from 1974 through 2004.
Guinness counted 453 piercings on Rolf Buchholz in 2012.
Lucky Diamond Rich's entire body is tattooed, including his eyelids and the inside of his mouth.
Hilton had over 7,500 hotels at the end of 2023.
Hartsfield-Jackson handled 104.7 million passengers in 2023, the world's highest total.
A single covalent bond consists of one shared pair of electrons: two electrons.
Chlorine has seventeen electrons; a chloride ion has one extra, giving eighteen.
A standard Rubik's Cube has six colours, one per face.
Hundreds of billions of LEGO bricks have been produced; the total increases every year.
Each chess player starts with eight pawns.
An eight-by-eight draughts board has 64 squares.
The main track has forty spaces, ten per colour.
The 1988 Honda RA168E was a six-cylinder turbocharged V6 engine.
The men's FIFA World Cup was held 22 times from 1930 through 2022.
French riders have won the Tour de France 36 times, most recently Bernard Hinault in 1985.
A marathon is 42.195 kilometres long.
Thirty-two countries took part in the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.
The 2026 World Cup was the first with 48 teams.
The Sun's volume is approximately 1.3 million times Earth's volume.
Jupiter rotates in approximately nine hours and 56 minutes, nearly ten hours.
Apollo 11 carried Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins: three crew members.
The IAU officially recognises five dwarf planets: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake.
Eleven additional moons announced on 16 March 2026 brought Saturn's known total to 285.
The ISS contains approximately thirteen kilometres of electrical wiring.
Earth orbits the Sun at an average speed of nearly thirty kilometres per second.
A light-year is approximately 9.46 trillion kilometres, or 9,460 billion kilometres.
Mars has two moons: Phobos and Deimos.
Uranus has thirteen known rings.
Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune all have rings.
Only Mercury and Venus orbit closer to the Sun than Earth.
The ISS orbits at an average altitude of approximately 400 kilometres.
The modern Georgian alphabet has 33 letters.
The Hebrew alphabet has 22 letters.
The Russian alphabet has 33 letters.
The modern Latin alphabet has 26 letters.
The UN has six official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish.
Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.
Under the binary convention, a gigabyte is 1,024 megabytes; the precise IEC names are gibibyte and mebibyte.
Apple sells a 20-watt USB-C Power Adapter for charging iPhones.
The first Android phone, the HTC Dream or T-Mobile G1, launched in 2008.
Paris and Brussels were connected by an international telephone line in 1887.
The HSL-Zuid railway is approximately 125 kilometres long.
The Shanghai Maglev reached 431 kilometres per hour in regular service before 2021; it subsequently ran at 300.
Rotterdam's metro has five lines: A, B, C, D and E.
Amsterdam's metro has five lines: 50, 51, 52, 53 and 54.
In 2025, the Paris Métro had sixteen lines: 1–14, plus 3bis and 7bis.
Heathrow has two parallel runways.
Schiphol has six runways.
The MTA counts 472 New York City Subway stations.
A Boeing 747 has eighteen wheels: sixteen on the main gear and two on the nose gear.
Robert Fulton tested his submarine Nautilus in France in 1800.
Two US Army aircraft completed the first aerial circumnavigation in 1924.
OICA reports over 85 million motor vehicles produced worldwide in 2022.
A polygon has n(n−3)/2 diagonals; a twelve-sided polygon has 54.
A full circle is defined as 360 degrees.
An octagon has eight sides.
An icosahedron has twenty faces and thirty edges.
